title: Structural Vulnerability in Latin America and the Caribbean
subtitle: Reproducible development analytics for comparing structural vulnerability, institutional constraints and socioeconomic risks across Latin America and the Caribbean.
author: Monica Cueto Tapia

coverage.complete_case_countries: 17 countries in the complete-case model sample

key_findings: Labor informality, unemployment and inequality are positively associated with structural vulnerability in the existing panel outputs.
Social protection coverage and GDP per capita are negatively associated with structural vulnerability.
Fixed-effects and two-way fixed-effects specifications are preferred for interpretation because they absorb time-invariant country characteristics and common year shocks.
The evidence is descriptive and associational, not causal.
Mechanism outputs suggest that social assistance and social insurance expansions are correlated across the region, limiting channel separation in the current panel.
Country event-study outputs are exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously.
methodology: Data audit for panel dimensions, country-year coverage, missingness, variable coverage, descriptive statistics and balance.
Structural vulnerability index using poverty, informality, social protection, GDP per capita, gender labor gap and unemployment components when available.
Baseline index averages available normalized components.
Sensitivity checks compare alternative weights and leave-one-component-out rankings.
Econometric evidence is descriptive and associational, not causal.
